subject: descriptor-hash
$comment: Positive cases carry computed values, made by two independent passes from PUBLIC-SPEC.md section 9 alone. Negative cases (reject, unverifiable) assert WHERE an input is refused, carry no computed value, and were written directly from the prose. METHOD: sort object keys as arrays of UTF-16 code units, recursively; emit with no whitespace; preserve array order; encode UTF-8; keccak256 over those bytes. Every positive case was validated against schema/prize-descriptor.json first, checked NFC, checked under the 16384-byte cap, and round-tripped: canon(parse(canon(x))) is byte-identical. 'canonical' carries the exact canonical text and is a second assertion, localising a failure to canonicalization or to hashing. Canonicalizer-level cases live in canonicalization.json. PROVENANCE, original cases: Pass A: Claude (an AI), in Python with a generic keccak256 library, no implementation consulted. Claude also drafted part of the prose, so a disagreement was to be read as possible evidence the text is unclear, not only as a miscomputation. Pass B, 2026-09-28: a second person, on a separate machine, with no access to this file or to pass A's method, notes or terminal, in JavaScript with ethers v6 for keccak256 and ABI encoding. Different language and libraries on each side, so a shared library bug cannot make both passes wrong in the same way. All 6 values agreed exactly. Pass B raised four spec-text gaps, none of them contradictions, each fixed in PUBLIC-SPEC.md without changing any value: abi.encode word widths and the empty-round value (section 3), excluded-range inclusivity (section 6), the schema file as the normative field set per schemaVersion, and the complete-JCS-plus-validating-layer shape (section 9). PROVENANCE, loader-rule cases added 2026-10-25 (parsing rules and the size stage): ten are negative or unverifiable. One, sizeAtCap, carries a computed hash. Pass A: Claude, with a scratch Python canonicalizer written from PUBLIC-SPEC.md section 9 and RFC 8785 only, keccak256 from a command-line tool over the exact bytes (checked twice, as text and as hex), canonical length 16384 bytes; the scratch script was deleted. Claude had previously worked on the operator's own descriptor pipeline, so this value was not treated as independent until pass B. Pass B, 2026-10-25: an AI (ChatGPT/Codex) on a hosted Linux workspace, not a human on a personal machine, recorded as such by decision of the project owner. It worked from a handoff holding only PUBLIC-SPEC.md (sha256 491da9ef...54fa), schema/prize-descriptor.json and RFC 8785, with the inputs under neutral labels, using JavaScript on Node 24, a hand-written RFC 8785 serializer, a JSON Schema 2020-12 validator, and two independent keccak256 libraries cross-checked; it shares no toolchain with pass A. sizeAtCap agreed exactly: 16384 bytes, the canonical sha256 and the hash. All ten stage readings agreed. Its three spec-text findings (the stage order, the verifier's NFC rejection, the UTF-8 and byte-order-mark rule) were fixed in PUBLIC-SPEC.md section 9; none changed a computed value. byteOrderMark was added with that fix, a negative case. Format: vectors/FORMAT.md.

cases.name: keysOutOfOrder
cases.description: Every key given in reverse order. The canonical form sorts them, so this must hash identically to the same descriptor written in any other order.

cases.name: nestedObjectUnsorted
cases.description: A specification object whose keys are also out of order. Asserts the sort recurses rather than applying only at the top level.

cases.name: nonAsciiNameNfc
cases.description: A CJK name. Already NFC with no decomposition, so it tests UTF-8 encoding of values rather than re-testing normalization. Keys stay ASCII, as constraint 1 requires.

cases.name: emptySpecificationValue
cases.description: A specification attribute present with an empty string. Legal, and must hash differently from absentSpecification below.

cases.name: absentSpecification
cases.description: The same descriptor with no specification key at all. Pairs with emptySpecificationValue: absence and an empty value are different bytes and different hashes, and absence is the ONLY empty representation since null is forbidden.

cases.name: imageOrderIsSignificant
cases.description: Three image references. Array order is display order and is part of the hash, unlike object keys which are sorted.

cases.name: unknownSchemaVersion
cases.description: schemaVersion the tool does not know. MUST report unverifiable, never reject: a rejection here is indistinguishable from a tampered descriptor (PUBLIC-SPEC.md §9). Requires version dispatch to run BEFORE schema validation, or the const:1 constraint turns this into a schema rejection.

cases.name: floatToken
cases.description: A float-valued number token. JSON Schema's integer type matches any number with a zero fractional part, and const:1 compares numerically, so 1.0 passes validation. Must be refused at parse time. Input is raw text because JSON.parse would destroy the distinction first.

cases.name: nullInOptionalField
cases.description: null as the value of an optional field. Absence is the only empty representation (PUBLIC-SPEC.md §9 constraint 5).

cases.name: nullInSpecificationValue
cases.description: null nested inside specification.

cases.name: unknownTopLevelField
cases.description: Field outside the fixed field set. A new field requires a schemaVersion bump.

cases.name: nonAsciiSpecificationKey
cases.description: Key outside ^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$. ASCII keys are what make JCS's UTF-16 key ordering unreachable.

cases.name: uppercaseLeadingSpecificationKey
cases.description: Key starting with an uppercase letter.

cases.name: unknownCategoryValue
cases.description: 'collectible' is not in the version-1 category enum, so schema validation rejects it.

cases.name: unknownConditionValue
cases.description: 'refurbished' is not in the version-1 condition enum, so schema validation rejects it.

cases.name: nonAsciiEnumValue
cases.description: A future append that violates the enumIdentifier pattern fails at the first descriptor using it.

cases.name: missingRequiredField
cases.description: condition omitted.

cases.name: duplicateImages
cases.description: Same reference twice. uniqueItems stops one image set having two canonical forms.

cases.name: emptyImagesArray
cases.description: At least one image is required.

cases.name: emptyName
cases.description: name must be non-empty. Distinct from an empty specification VALUE, which is legal.

cases.name: nfdInName
cases.description: Name in NFD. Schema-valid, hashes differently from NFC, visually identical. JCS does not normalize and will not warn. Written as \u escapes so a normalizing editor cannot silently turn this case into a no-op.

cases.name: nfdInSpecificationValue
cases.description: NFD nested in a specification value. The check must recurse, not just cover top-level strings.

cases.name: sizeAtCap
cases.description: Every field within its schema limits, astral-plane text throughout, and a canonical form of exactly 16384 UTF-8 bytes: the largest descriptor that has a hash. The cap counts canonical bytes, not characters (PUBLIC-SPEC.md 9).

cases.name: sizeOverCap
cases.description: sizeAtCap with one more byte in a specification value: 16385 canonical bytes. Every field is still within its schema limits, so only the size stage can refuse it.

cases.name: duplicateTopLevelKey
cases.description: name appears twice. An ordinary parser keeps one silently; I-JSON forbids duplicates (PUBLIC-SPEC.md 9).

cases.name: duplicateNestedKey
cases.description: A key repeated inside specification: duplicates are refused in any object, not only at the top level.

cases.name: loneHighSurrogate
cases.description: A high surrogate escape with no low surrogate after it: not well-formed Unicode, which I-JSON forbids.

cases.name: loneLowSurrogate
cases.description: A low surrogate escape with no high surrogate before it, here in an image reference.

cases.name: integerAtSafeLimit
cases.description: schemaVersion 2^53: an integer token, but outside the safe range, so refused at parse before version dispatch can see it.

cases.name: exponentToken
cases.description: schemaVersion written 1e0: a number token with an exponent, refused whatever its value.

cases.name: largestSafeVersionUnknown
cases.description: schemaVersion 2^53 - 1: a safe integer, so it parses, and a version this tool does not know, so it is unverifiable rather than rejected.

cases.name: stringSchemaVersion
cases.description: schemaVersion "1": not an integer, so not a version at all. Schema rejection, never unverifiable.

cases.name: booleanSchemaVersion
cases.description: schemaVersion true: not an integer either. Schema rejection.

cases.name: byteOrderMark
cases.description: A valid descriptor preceded by U+FEFF, the byte-order mark. The text must be UTF-8 without one (PUBLIC-SPEC.md 9); a decoder that strips it silently would hash what a strict one rejects.
